subject.title: fix: reject malformed UTF-8 in fetched web content responses

question: Should link understanding remain available for declared non-UTF-8 web content, or should it intentionally fail closed on every response that is not valid UTF-8?
rationale: The proposed one-line change selects a user-visible availability-versus-integrity policy, while the current fetch path accepts broad text media types and does not define a UTF-8-only contract.

options.title: Use a charset-aware decode policy
options.body: Honor a supported declared charset and reject malformed content only when it cannot be decoded under the documented policy.

options.title: Adopt UTF-8-only decoding
options.body: Keep fatal UTF-8 decoding, but explicitly approve the compatibility break and add coverage and documentation for whole-link skipping.

recommendation.title: Use a charset-aware decode policy
recommendation.body: Honor a supported declared charset and reject malformed content only when it cannot be decoded under the documented policy.

likelyOwner.reason: dasilva333 introduced the link-understanding runner and is the strongest history-based owner for its content contract.
